To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of heterozygosity at the TIG1, RB1, PTEN and cyclin D2 loci is detectable in the plasma of breast cancer patients.

loss of heterozygosity on circulating tumor DNA in breast cancer patients is more frequent in the fraction containing shorter DNA molecules, and that loss of heterositygosity at the cyclin D 2 locus is associated with shorter overall survival.

we have shown that LOH on circulating tumor DNA is more frequently detectable in the fraction of short DNA fragments, and that LOH at the cyclin D1 locus is associated with poor survival of breast cancer patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a molecular marker for breast cancer progression.
the detection of circulating DNA and the determination of the prognostic value in breast cancer patients.
the development of new methods to detect and characterize circulating cell free DNA (cfDNA) in plasma of cancer patients and to identify tumor-specific alterations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fractionated cell-free tumor DNA analysis is a promising approach in breast cancer diagnostics and prognostics.
the detection of circulating tumor DNA in plasma of cancer patients is feasible, and the detection of LOH at the tumor suppressor genes cyclin D2 and TIG1 is of prognostic relevance.

LOH on circulating cell-free DNA may provide tumor specific information on breast cancer, and that the improved detection of LOHS on cell-free DNA may become an important tool in the diagnosis of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that LOH on cellfree DNA is a promising biomarker to detect tumor progression in breast cancer.
we found that LOH on circulating cell-free tumor DNA is detectable in breast cancer and that it is associated with poor clinical outcome.

the fractionation of cell-free DNA is an important tool to improve the detection of LOH in plasma of patients with primary breast tumors and may be useful for the detection of circulating tumor DNA after chemotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LOH in cell free DNA can be detected by fractionating the DNA and using microsatellites as markers.
the detection of loss of heterozygosity in the fraction containing small DNA molecules in the blood of breast cancer patients is more sensitive than in the fraction with the long DNA molecules.
circulating cell-free DNA is an easily accessible and reliable source for the analysis of genetic alterations in patients with breast cancer.
